purpose: Test whether two exact sparse remesh metrics assemble across a shared edge without losing chain adjointness, positivity or macroelement locality.

assembly.conclusion: Standard additive macroelement assembly preserves the exact metric pullback, weighted-adjoint restriction, chain map and self-adjoint reconstruction identities across the shared edge.

positivity.argument: Each assembled fine metric is a sum of positive local Gram forms. Every global degree of freedom lies in at least one macroelement, so the sum is positive definite; full matrix rank is independently reported.

locality.meaning: No coupling directly joins the two centre stars or faces belonging exclusively to different macroelements. Shared vertices and the shared edge mediate assembly.

verdict: The sparse macroelement escape survives the first overlap test. Two locally exact remesh blocks assemble into positive global metrics while retaining cochain transport, weighted adjointness and energy-orthogonal reconstruction; arbitrary meshes and conditioning remain open.
